did_you_know.text: Did you know? The psalm opens with a call to praise the Lord and presents singing as good, pleasant, and fitting.
Did you know? The rebuilding of Jerusalem and the gathering of Israel’s exiles appear together as descriptions of the Lord’s work on behalf of his people.
Did you know? The Lord is described as a healer of the brokenhearted and one who binds up their sorrows, meaning that he brings healing and comfort to the afflicted.
Did you know? According to the psalm, the Lord counts the number of the stars and calls each one by name, expressing his complete knowledge.
Did you know? The Lord’s greatness is described together with his understanding, which is beyond measure.
Did you know? The psalm contrasts the Lord’s support for the humble with his casting the wicked down to the ground.
Did you know? The Lord’s care includes the animals as well: he provides food for the livestock and even for the young ravens that call to him.
Did you know? The psalm emphasizes that the Lord does not take primary pleasure in the strength of a horse or in human physical power.
Did you know? Jerusalem’s blessing includes strengthening the bars of its gates and blessing the children within it, portraying a protected city and a blessed community.

Did you know? After describing the Lord’s control over nature, the psalm emphasizes that he declares his word, statutes, and judgments to Jacob and Israel; in this way, it presents the Torah as a special gift to Israel.
